items.text: Proof (continued): $f'\colon X'\to Y'$ compatible with the descent data is a subscheme $Z'\subset P'=X'\times_{S'}Y'$ (graph) whose two inverse images in $P''$ coincide; if $Z'$ is retrocompact it descends to $Z\subset P$.
$Z\to X$ is an isomorphism after base change, hence an isomorphism. Retrocompactness holds if $Y$ is quasi-separated over $S$ (sections are quasi-compact).
General case
$S$ affine, $Y=\bigcup Y_i$ affine, $X'_i=f'^{-1}(Y'_i)$: stable under descent, so $X'_i=g^{-1}X_i$; $X'_i\to Y'_i$ descends ($Y_i$ affine); the maps $X_i\to Y$ glue by uniqueness.
Hence for $S'\to S$ faithfully flat quasi-compact, $X\mapsto(X',\text{descent datum})$ from schemes over $S$ to schemes over $S'$ with descent data is fully faithful; effectivity is subtle.
Effective for relatively affine schemes: affine schemes over $S$ $\simeq$ affine schemes over $S'$ with descent data.
Descent of immersions
$f$ is an open immersion (closed immersion, quasi-compact immersion) $\iff$ $f'$ is.
Closed case: $X'\subset Y'$ closed with equal inverse images in $Y''$; $X\to Y$ is a monomorphism (subobject); the descended subscheme $T\subset Y$ and $X$ are equal after base change, hence equal.
For immersions in general: $X=\bigcup X_i$ (finite unions of affines); each $X_i\to Y$ is an immersion; but a filtering union of locally closed immersions need not be locally closed:
counterexample: the disjoint union of all closed points of the line $\to$ the line (dense image). Descent of immersions without compactness left open.
Closure of an image: reformulation of the lemma
$f\colon Z\to S$ quasi-compact, $s\in S$:
s\in\overline{f(Z)}\iff\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}\cap f(Z)\neq\varnothing\iff\exists\,t\in f(Z):\ s\in\overline{\{t\}}
A=f(Z),\ B=S\setminus f(Z):\qquad s\in\overline A\iff\exists\,s'\leadsto s,\ s'\in A;\qquad s\in\operatorname{int}B\iff\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}\subset B
Generalizing implies open
$f\colon Z\to S$ generalizing, $Z,S$ affine: the image is stable under generalization; it is open if it is constructible (image and complement both images of quasi-compact morphisms).

Image of a morphism of finite presentation is constructible: pass to $S$ noetherian, induct on $S$; at a maximal point $s$ either $Z_s=\varnothing$ (then empty over a neighborhood) or $Z_s\neq\varnothing$ (then non-empty over a neighborhood), by passage to the limit.
Hence a generalizing morphism locally of finite presentation is open (used for $X\times Y\to Y$ over a field).
Summary of descent

Properties that descend by faithfully flat quasi-compact base change: closed/open/quasi-compact immersion, proper, separated, finite type, locally of (finite) presentation, quasi-compact, quasi-separated, universally open, universally generalizing; for modules: finite type, finite presentation, free, locally free of rank $n$, invertible.
Counterexample: projective and quasi-projective do not descend (not even Zariski local on the base).

\text{0-descent: }\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(M',N')\qquad\text{1-descent: }\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}(M',N')\rightrightarrows\operatorname{Hom}(M'',N'')\ \text{exact}

2-descent: $M'$ with a descent datum $p_1^*M'\simeq p_2^*M'$ satisfying the cocycle condition on $S'''$ comes from some $M$ over $S$ (equivalence of categories, not an exact sequence of isomorphism classes). Topoi would need higher descent data.
Consequences: exactness for submodules and quotients, closed subschemes ($M=\mathcal O_S$), retrocompact subschemes, open subschemes; hence 1-descent for relative schemes.
\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X',Y')\rightrightarrows\operatorname{Hom}(X'',Y'')\ \text{exact};\qquad \text{effectivity fails in general for schemes}
Effective descent for affine schemes
$S'\to S$ faithfully flat quasi-compact is of effective descent for schemes affine over the base.
Affine over $S$ $\leftrightarrow$ quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebras $\mathcal A$. The multiplication is a map
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\ \text{compatible with descent data}\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{descends (1-descent)}
Associativity, commutativity, unit: diagrams commuting after base change commute (0-descent); the unit section is stable under the descent data.
So 2-descent for modules gives 2-descent for quasi-coherent commutative algebras, hence for affine schemes.
